A_target.statement:
Let $f$ be [[Definition:Continuous on Closed Interval|continuous]] on $\closedint a b$ and [[Definition:Differentiable on Interval|differentiable]] on $\openint a b$.
Then:
:$\exists \xi \in \openint a b: \map {f'} \xi = \dfrac {\map f b - \map f a} {b - a}$

B_source.statement:
Let $g$ be continuous on $\closedint a b$ and differentiable on $\openint a b$ with $\map g a = \map g b$.
Then:
:$\exists \xi \in \openint a b: \map {g'} \xi = 0$

substitutions.the horizontal chord g(a) = g(b): the secant through (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b))

object_map.reformulation: Subtract the secant line so that the endpoint values become equal, reducing to the horizontal case.

validity_conditions: Subtracting an affine function preserves continuity and differentiability.
The affine correction must be chosen so that g(a) = g(b) exactly.
proof_plan:
Let:
:$\map g x = \map f x - \dfrac {\map f b - \map f a} {b - a} \paren {x - a}$

$g$ is continuous on $\closedint a b$ and differentiable on $\openint a b$, as a difference of such functions.
Also $\map g a = \map f a$ and $\map g b = \map f b - \paren {\map f b - \map f a} = \map f a$.
By [[Rolle's Theorem]], there exists $\xi \in \openint a b$ with $\map {g'} \xi = 0$.

As $\map {g'} \xi = \map {f'} \xi - \dfrac {\map f b - \map f a} {b - a}$:
:$\map {f'} \xi = \dfrac {\map f b - \map f a} {b - a}$
which is the [[Mean Value Theorem]], with Rolle's Theorem as the case $\map f a = \map f b$.
{{qed}}
